title: Dashboard & discuss-list UI consistency (ref segments + scroll containment)
summary: Make dashboard Latest-Completed / New-Added cards use the same clickable+copy Fxxx/Pxxx/Txxx segmented ref as WorkTree, and fix Pi discuss/list commands' scroll containment so long lists stay in their viewport.
description:
F005 improvements sub-phase for two concrete UI consistency bugs discovered during the P069 resume-awareness work:

(1) Dashboard "Latest completed tasks" (packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/latest-completed-tasks.tsx) and "New Added Tasks" (packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/new-added-tasks.tsx) render only `EntityBadge type=task` (Txxx) + `ParentBadge` (Pxxx(Fxxx)) — they do NOT show the full clickable Fxxx/Pxxx/Txxx segmented reference with per-segment copy buttons that the WorkTree cards (packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree.tsx) and the entity detail pages use. Goal: give both dashboard cards the SAME segmented ref header as the WorkTree — each segment (Fxxx / Pxxx(Fxxx) / Txxx) clickable (navigates to the entity) and each carrying a copy button for the number and the shortId. Reuse the existing reusable ref component (CompositeRef / segment + CopyableBadge in packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/ui/badges.tsx: CopyableBadge, EntityPathBadge, ShortIdBadge, formatEntityPath). If no single reusable segmented-ref component exists that does clickable-segments + copy for number+shortId, create one and use it consistently across WorkTree, entity detail pages, and these two dashboard cards so the header is identical everywhere.

(2) In Pi (packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts), `/planner feature discuss`, `/planner phase discuss`, `/planner task discuss` (and any sibling command that populates a long entity list) render a list of features/phases/tasks that overflows the available height. It is scrollable, but when the user scrolls to the bottom the cursor/selection escapes the list viewport instead of keeping the items scrolled within the container. Must inspect ALL commands that populate a list view (feature discuss, phase discuss, task discuss, feature list, phase list, task list, handoff list, and any other list-rendering path) and fix the scroll containment / focus trapping so the list stays within its scroll area and items scroll up when at the bottom. Likely requires a shared scrollable-list component in the pi-adapter UI surface (ctx.ui) rather than per-command ad-hoc rendering.

Out of scope: changing the Web UI header (already addressed by P070/F005 and P071/F005); changing the planner core data model; GSD.

This phase deliberately lives OUTSIDE the P069 resume-awareness sequence — P069 (T296/T297/T298) and the P060 CI task (T258) take precedence and are worked first, per project instruction.

tasks.title: Fix Pi discuss/list command scroll containment (cursor escapes list at bottom)
tasks.description:
Issue 2 (P072/F005): In Pi (packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts), `/planner feature discuss`, `/planner phase discuss`, `/planner task discuss` (and any sibling command that populates a long entity list) render a list of features/phases/tasks that overflows the available height. It is scrollable, but when the user scrolls to the bottom the cursor/selection escapes the list viewport instead of keeping the items scrolled within the container — i.e. the list is not properly contained in its own scrollable surface.

Work:
1. Locate every command handler that renders a long entity list: `feature discuss`, `phase discuss`, `task discuss`, `feature list`, `phase list`, `task list`, `handoff list`, and any other list-rendering path in packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts (search discuss/list/scroll/overflow). Confirm which share a rendering path and which are ad-hoc.
2. Determine the Pi UI surface used (ctx.ui.* list/scroll primitives) and where the scroll container / focus handling lives — the bug is likely a missing `overflow` containment, a focus/selection trap that lets the cursor leave the list, or a container that grows with content instead of clipping to a max height.
3. Introduce or reuse a single shared scrollable-list component for the pi-adapter command UI so ALL list-populating commands keep their items inside a fixed-height scroll area (scroll up when at the bottom; cursor/focus stays within the list). Apply it to every command found in step 1 — do NOT fix only discuss while leaving list/handoff broken.
4. Verify the long-list behavior in the real Pi harness: scrolling to the bottom keeps items within the viewport and does not let the cursor escape the page.

Code references: packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts discuss handlers (PLANNER_COMMAND_COMPLETIONS list ~118-141 incl. "feature discuss"/"phase discuss"/"task discuss"/"handoff list"; command dispatch at ~1150-1164; handler bodies around 1239+ for project/feature/phase/task discuss). The list UI is rendered through the extension ctx.ui surface.

Tests: if the pi-adapter has unit/integration tests for the discuss/list rendering (packages/pi-adapter/test), extend or add coverage for long-list scroll containment; otherwise document the manual verification via the real Pi harness (`pi --no-extensions -e ...` or the user's launch) since this is a TUI scroll-focus behavior. Run `pnpm --filter @agent-plan/pi-adapter build` + its test script green.

---
**Completion summary:**
Completed T306 (P072/F005) — Pi discuss/list command scroll containment via pagination (no custom component).

Root cause: Pi's `ctx.ui.select` (ExtensionUIDialogOptions) exposes only `signal`/`timeout` — no max-height/scroll option. Long option lists (every feature/phase/task via the `Pick a X` helpers) overflow the TUI viewport and the selection cursor can escape the list at the bottom. The read-only `feature list` / `handoff list` commands overflow via `ctx.ui.notify(join)` as well.

Approach (per user: paginate, max 10 items/page, NOT a custom `ctx.ui.custom` component):
- New `packages/pi-adapter/src/ui/paginate.ts`:
  - `paginatedSelect<T>(ctx, { title, items, render, pageSize=10, allowPrev=true })` — short lists (≤10) fall through to a single `ctx.ui.select` (zero regression on small projects); long lists page with a trailing `› Next page (x/N)` sentinel and a `‹ Prev page` row, title shows `— page x/N —`. Maps the chosen label back to the entity via `labels.indexOf(chosen)` (same mechanism the old code used).
  - `paginatedNotify(ctx, { title, lines, pageSize=10 })` — short lists single `notify`; long lists page with a `— title — page x/N —` header and an `input` prompt (`Enter = next page · q = quit`).
- `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts`:
  - `pickFeature` (1288), `pickPhase` (1302), `pickTask` (1315) → `paginatedSelect`. These are called from ~20 discuss/add flows, so the fix covers all of them at once.
  - `feature list` (1576) and `handoff list` (2308) → `paginatedNotify`.
  - Menu action `select` (1189) left unchanged — fixed small list, not the bug.

Verification:
- `pnpm --filter @agent-plan/pi-adapter check` clean; `build` clean (emits `dist/ui/paginate.js`).
- pi-adapter unit suite **55/55** (47 existing + 8 new), **fail 0**. New `test/paginate.test.mjs` covers: short-list single-call passthrough, long-list forward paging returns correct later-page item, Prev navigation, every page bounded ≤ pageSize, empty items → null/no-op, and `paginatedNotify` short/long/empty behavior.
- Confirmed `rg`/`rg`-style edits applied by reading the wired call sites (6 of them) before trusting the tool result.

Manual TUI verification still recommended in the real Pi (`pi --no-extensions -e packages/pi-adapter/dist/index.js`): a long feature/phase/task list now pages with Next/Prev and the cursor stays inside the viewport; `feature list` / `handoff list` page with headers.

No commit, no bundle copy (adapter extension, dist already rebuilt; working tree only). P072 now has all tasks done (T305, T308, T306); T307 was reclassified to P069 (already complete). Per P072's original precedence note, P060 T258 remains the next pending item after this P072 work was pulled forward.

tasks.title: Enforce parent feature + phase read on task start and resume
tasks.description:
The requirement to read the parent feature AND phase before starting or resuming a task IS imposed at the protocol/description level, but it is unreliable and must be improved. Verified by reading the actual code paths:

- `task_start` TOOL (pi-adapter packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:4214, description at 4216) says: "BEFORE calling, read feature_get(full=true), phase_get(full=true), then task_get(full=true)." plan-mcp's task_start tool (packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:1249) carries the equivalent instruction. So the feature read is listed, BUT because there is no read-tracking the requirement is not reliably honored — an agent can skip the feature read, and nothing enforces it.
- `task_start` TOOL (pi-adapter :4214) also assembles and returns the parent context block (phaseContext via loadPhaseWithRequirements + linkedRequirementsForFeature, ~4284-4305) AFTER the state change, so the agent receives feature+phase+requirements even if it skipped the read.
- It is NOT code-enforced: no guard refuses to start/resume if the phase/feature were not read. checkExplicitTaskStart (packages/plan-core/src/task-selection.ts:39) validates ONLY eligibility (existence, startable status, parent availability, dependencies) and never inspects read state. A repo-wide grep for any read-tracking/guard (readRefs|markRead|readState|readTracking|lastRead|readSet|hasRead|readGuard) returned NOTHING.
- INCONSISTENCY: the `/planner task start` COMMAND (packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:2160, `if (b === "start")`) does NOT impose reading at all — no "read first" instruction and it does not even call checkExplicitTaskStart. The command path enforces less than the tool path.

REQUIRED IMPROVEMENTS (this task):
1. Reliably impose reading the FEATURE (not just the phase/task). The feature read is currently only text in the description; make it enforced with tracking so an agent cannot silently skip it.
2. DEDUPLICATE reads: reading the parent feature + phase must happen ONCE per phase (or on resume), NOT once per task. If a phase has 10 tasks, the agent reads feature+phase a single time and is not forced to re-read for each of the 10 tasks. Re-read is required only on resume or when switching to a different phase/feature (the read-set should be keyed by phase/feature identity, and invalidated on resume or phase/feature change). This avoids 10 redundant read round-trips for 10 sibling tasks.

Goal: make reading the parent feature AND phase a consistent, deduplicated precondition across ALL start/resume entry points (the /planner task start command 2160, pi-adapter task_start tool 4214, plan-mcp task_start tool 1249, and task_switch/resume pi-adapter 4094 / plan-mcp 1140).

Implementation considerations: introduce a read-tracking guard (analogous to the existing NO ACTIVE TASK advisory) that records which feature/phase refs were read by the agent, keyed per phase/feature so repeated task starts in the same phase do not re-trigger the read; warn or block task_start/task_switch/resume when the target task's parent feature+phase are not in the read set, unless already read for that phase (or on resume / phase change). Apply consistently across both harness tools, the /planner task start command, and the resume paths; add tests.

Edge cases: resume of a paused task (pauseSnapshot present) re-requires reading feature+phase; task_switch should require reading both source and target parents (deduplicated per phase); deviation/temporary tasks still require reading the target's parent; agents that already read via the tools pass the guard without re-reading for sibling tasks.
tasks.notes:
T307 (P072/F005) implemented & verified.

Root cause of the earlier stall: the edit tool silently failed (returned the injected "Reminder" without writing) on packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts because the markRead oldText used `.filter((p) => p.featureId ...)` while the real file uses `.filter((phase) => phase.featureId ...)`; a single bad match aborts the whole multi-edit batch, so none of the 6 markRead calls landed. Fixed with a targeted Node patch script (first-occurrence only for feature-show, leaving feature-delete untouched).

Implementation:
- NEW packages/plan-core/src/read-tracking.ts: module-level Set<{featureId?,phaseId}> + helpers markFeatureRead/ markPhaseRead/ markTaskRead/ hasReadParents/ invalidateReads/ parentReadAdvisory/ readTrackingSnapshot; exported via index.ts.
- Wired markRead into 6 get/show tools: pi-adapter feature_get:3164, phase_get:3445, task_get:3763; plan-mcp planner-feature-show:466, planner-phase-show:654, planner-task-show:825 (feature-delete:549 deliberately left unmarked).
- Wired non-blocking parent-read enforcement: pi-adapter command-start notify:2180 (hasReadParents), task_start return:4330, task_switch return:4214 (parentReadAdvisory → warn + structured readRequired); plan-mcp planner-task-start return:1360, planner-task-switch return:1241.
- Wired invalidateReads() into task_pause in both: pi-adapter:4076, plan-mcp:1115 (so resume requires re-read).
- NEW packages/plan-core/test/read-tracking.test.mjs: 7/7 (dedup, orphan phase, invalidate).

Verification: plan-core full suite 9 failures = pre-existing T253 baseline (no new); pi-adapter 55/55 fail 0; plan-mcp 50/50 fail 0; both adapter check+build clean. No commit. Manual TUI/CLI verification of the READ REQUIRED warning recommended (module-level state, like T306).

tasks.title: Dashboard card ref tooltips + right-aligned status + back-nav scroll restoration
tasks.description:

Apply each as a native `title` attribute on the corresponding segment's `<Link>`/`<span>`: Fxxx → feature name, Pxxx → phase name, Txxx → task title. Native `title` (no new Tooltip component) keeps it consistent with `CopyableBadge`/`HandoffBadge`/resume-required icon. Additive — no behavior change when names are omitted, so WorkTree/header callers keep working unchanged.

2) **Right-aligned status** on the dashboard Latest Completed / New Added cards — mirror WorkTree's pattern (work-tree-rows.tsx:389 `sm:flex-row sm:justify-between` + `flex-1` left + `shrink-0` right). 3) **Back-navigation scroll restoration** — router is data-mode `createBrowserRouter` (src/app/router.tsx:44, react-router-dom 7.18). Page scrolls via window (base.css:18 `.page-shell { min-height: 100vh }`, no nested scroll container). Render `<ScrollRestoration />` once in `RootRoute` (src/app/root.tsx:18) so window scroll is saved per `location.key` and restored on POP (back/forward), scrolling to top on PUSH. ~2 lines (import + element).

tasks.title: Fix header Active-task click: ?locate=xxx stripped and no scroll
tasks.description:
Bug segnalato dall'utente (2026-08-22): cliccando il task **Active** (in-progress) nell'header della Web UI, il link aggiunge `?locate=<taskRef>` per scrollare l'albero fino al task, ma la pagina **rimuove i query param** e **non esegue lo scroll**. Da investigare: componente header Active-task (probabilmente FocusTaskRow / TaskFocusHeader in packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx) e la logica di scroll-on-locate (hook useLocate / effetto su ?locate in packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/route.tsx o hook dedicato). Sospetto: la navigazione verso il link riscrive l'URL senza preservare i search param, oppure l'effetto di scroll si attiva prima che il param sia presente / viene pulito da un replace. Comportamento atteso: clic sull'Active task → URL mantiene ?locate=<ref> e l'albero scrolla fino al task corrispondente (evidenziato). Non è un code edit delle regole planner; è un fix Web UI. Verifica: dev-server Vite (:5175) + browser-tools (puppeteer) oppure plan-server su porta libera; hard reload per bypassare cache. Nessun commit senza approvazione.

---
**Completion summary:**
Fixed header Active-task "locate" (FocusTaskRow → navigate(`/?locate=T${task.number}`), app-shell.tsx:53) stripping ?locate before scroll. Root cause: in packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree.tsx the locate effect read phases.flatMap(...).find(t => t.number === locateNum); when phases was still empty at the first effect run (fresh dashboard mount or cross-route navigation into /?locate=…), found was null and the if(!found) branch deleted the param immediately (work-tree.tsx:207-213), so when phases later arrived locateNum was already null and no scroll happened — exactly the reported "removes params and not scroll". Fix: in the !found branch, return early (keep the param) while phases.length === 0 so the effect retries once data is present; only strip when phases is populated and the task genuinely doesn't exist. Verified: pnpm --filter @agent-plan/web-ui check (tsc) clean. No commit. Browser smoke (Vite :5175 / plan-server) recommended but not blocking.
tasks.notes: CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (supersedes the earlier partial diagnosis). Earlier fix only deferred the ?locate param strip when phases were empty, but locate STILL failed. Real root cause: app/root.tsx mounts React Router's <ScrollRestoration />. The locate effect stripped ?locate via setSearchParams(..., { replace: true }), which React Router treats as a navigation; <ScrollRestoration /> then reset window scroll to top, cancelling the scrollIntoView/scrollTo to the task. The param was removed but the page ended at top. Fix (work-tree.tsx): added clearLocateParam() that strips ?locate via window.history.replaceState (NO router navigation, so <ScrollRestoration /> does not fire) and replaced both setSearchParams locate-strips; removed now-unused setSearchParams setter. Verified: pnpm --filter @agent-plan/web-ui check + build clean. NOT browser-verified (ScrollRestoration behavior needs a real browser); logic confirmed by the ScrollRestoration-on-navigation mechanism.

tasks.title: Enforce phase/feature linked-requirements read on task start and resume
tasks.description:
Estensione di T307 (P072/F005): il read-enforcement attuale traccia SOLO feature+fase. Estendere l'obbligo (advisory non-bloccante, stile NO ACTIVE TASK) anche ai requirements collegati alla FASE e, se presenti, alla FEATURE.

Decisioni approvate dall'utente (2026-08-22):
(a) Richiedere i requirements della fase; richiedere anche quelli della feature SE la feature ha requirements collegati (linkedRequirementsForFeature restituisce [] se assenti → vacuo).
(b) Lettura ESPICITA A PARTE: NON auto-derivare il requirement-read dalla lettura della fase/feature/task. L'unico tool di lettura requirements negli adapter e' requirement_list (non esiste requirement_get) → agganciare markRequirementRead a requirement_list (lettura esplicita dell'elenco requirements).
(c) Entrambi gli harness (pi-adapter + plan-mcp), simmetrici a T307.

Modello dati (verificato): Requirement top-level; RequirementSchema.linkedPhaseIds (schema.ts:363) collega requirement→fase. PlanStore.linkedRequirementsForPhase(phaseId) (plan-store.ts:1455) e linkedRequirementsForFeature(featureId) (1459). task-context.ts buildPhaseContextBlock gia' mostra i requirements nel context (ma cio' NON conta come read esplicito, per (b)).

Piano implementazione:
1. read-tracking.ts: aggiungere `requirements: Set<string>`, `markRequirementRead(reqId)`, `hasReadRequirements(reqIds: string[]): boolean`, `requirementReadAdvisory(reqIds: string[]): string` (vuoto se tutti letti, altrimenti avviso READ REQUIRED requirements, stile parentReadAdvisory).
